With reference to Menkes disease, consider the following statements:
1. It is a genetic disorder that affects the body’s ability to absorb and distribute copper.
2. It primarily leads to excessive accumulation of copper in vital organs like the liver and brain.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution_text: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration recently approved the Zycubo (copper histidinate) as the first Streatment for Menkes disease in pediatric patients. Menkes disease is a rare inherited genetic disorder caused by mutations affecting copper transport in the body. It results in poor absorption and improper distribution of copper, leading to deficiency in varioIus tissues, particularly affecting the brain and nervous system. This makes Statement 1 correct. V In contrast, Statement 2 is incorrect because excessive accumulation of copper in organs is characteristic of Wilson’s disease, not Menkes disease. Hence, only Statement 1 is correct.

questions.question_text:
With reference to the Fundamental Rights available in India, consider the following:
1. Right to Privacy
2. Protection against arrest and detention
3. Right to freedom of speech and expression
Which of the above rights are available only to citizens?
questions.solution_text: Fundamental Rights in India are categorized based on whether they apply only to citizens or to everyone (citizens and foreigners alike) within the country. Those fundamental rights that are available to citizens only: It belongs to a specific set of articles—15, 16, 19, 29, and 30—that are reserved exclusively for Indian citizens. Hence, option 3 is correct. Those fundamental rights which are available to both citizens and foreigners: Equality before law and equal protection of laws (Article 14) Protection in respect of conviction for offences (Article 20) Protection of life and personal liberty (Article 21). Right to Privacy has been declared as a fundamental right by Supreme Court under Article 21. Hence, option 1 is not correct. Right to education (Article 21A) 1 www.visionias.in ©Vision IAS Protection against arrest and detention in certain cases (Article 22). Hence, option 2 is not correct. Prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour (Article 23). Prohibition of employment of children in factories etc., (Article 24). Freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion (Article 25). Freedom to manage religious affairs (Article 26). Freedom from payment of taxes for promotion of any religion (Article 27). Freedom from attending religious instruction or worship in certain educational institutions (Article 28). S

questions.question_text:
With reference to the Preamble of the Constitution of India, consider the following statements:
1. It is based on the ‘Objective Resolution’ moved by Jawaharlal Nehru in 1946.
2. It was enacted before the rest of the Constitution by the Constituent Assembly.
3. It states that the Constitution derives its authority from the people of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution_text: The Preamble to the Indian Constitution is based on the ‘Objective Resolution’ drafted and moved by Jawaharlal Nehru on 13 December 1946. It was adopted unaAnimously by the Constituent Assembly on 22 January 1947. Hence statement 1 is correct. After adopting the Preamble, it stands as part of the Constitution. Therefore, the current opinion on the Preamble held by the Supreme Court is in consonance with the opinion of the founding fathers. I The Preamble was enacted only after the rest of the Constitution was enacted by the Constituent N Assembly. Hence statement 2 is not correct. The reason for enacting the Preamble at the end was to ensure that it was in conformity with the Constitution as adopted by the Constituent Assembly. O It states that the constitution derives its authority from the people of India. Therefore it reveals the source of authority of the constitution. Hence statement 3 is correct.

questions.question_text:
With reference to the Preamble of the Constitution of India, consider the following objectives:
1. Political Justice
2. Economic Liberty
3. Equality of Status
4. Unity and Integrity of the Nation
How many of the above objectives are stated in the Preamble?
questions.solution_text: The preamble of the Indian Constitution- • I WE, THE PEOPLE OF INDIA, having solemnly resolved to constitute India into a SOVEREIGN S SOCIALIST SECULAR DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC and to secure to all its citizens: JUSTICE, social, economic, and political; Hence option 1 is correct. LIBERTY of thought, expression, belief, faith, and worship; Hence option 2 is not correct. I EQUALITY of status and of opportunity; and to promote among them all, Hence option 3 is V correct. FRATERNITY assuring the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the Nation; Hence option 4 is correct. IN OUR CONSTITUENT ASSEMBLY this twenty-sixth day of November 1949, do HEREBY ADOPT, ENACT AND GIVE TO OURSELVES THIS CONSTITUTION. Preamble reveals the source of authority of the constitution which is "the authority from the people of India". It declares the nature of the Indian state as sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic, and republican polity. It specifies justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity as the objectives of the constitution. It also mentions the date of adoption of the constitution which is November 26, 1949

questions.question_text:
With reference to laws enacted to implement the Directive Principles of State Policy, consider the following statements:
1. 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act gives effect to Article 40.
2. The Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 and the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980, enactments give effect to Article 50
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution_text: Statement 2 is not correct: Article 48A seeks to protect and improve the environment and to safeguard forests and wildlife. Article 48 seeks to organize agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines and prohibit the slaughter of cows, calves, and other milch and draught cattle, and 2 www.visionias.in ©Vision IAS improve their breeds. Hence, the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 and the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980, have been enacted to give effect to Article 48A, not Article 50. Statement 1 is correct: Article 40 seeks to organize village panchayats and endow them with the necessary powers and authority to enable them to function as units of self-government. Hence, the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act has been passed to give effect to Article 40.

questions.question_text: If the President of India exercises his power as provided under Article 359 of the Constitution, then

options.label: A
options.option_text: the President can promulgate ordinance for any state.

options.label: B
options.option_text: the powers of High Courts are subsumed by the Supreme Court.

options.label: C
options.option_text: the President is empowered to suspend the enforcement of some Fundamental Rights.

options.label: D
options.option_text: he may extend National Emergency only to few parts of the country and not the entire country.

questions.solution_text: Article 359 authorises the President to suspend the right to move any court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights during a National Emergency. This means that under Article 359, the Fundamental Rights as such are not suspended, but only their enforcement. The said rights are theoretically alive but the right to seek remedy is suspended. TheS suspension of enforcement relates to only those Fundamental Rights that are specified in the Presidential Order. Further, the suspension could be for the period during the operation of emergency or for a shorter period as mentioned in the order, and the suspension order may exteAnd to the whole or any part of the country. It should be laid before each House of Parliament for approval. Hence, only option (c) is correct. The 44th Amendment Act of 1978 restricted the scope of Article 359 in two ways. Firstly, the President cannot suspend the right to move the Court for the enforcement of fundamental rights I guaranteed by Articles 20 to 21. Secondly, only those laws which are related with the emergency are N protected from being challenged and not other laws and the executive action taken only under such a law, is protected. Article 359 operates in case of both when National Emergency is declared on grounds of war or external aggression as welOl as on the ground of armed rebellion. Article 359 may extend to the entire country or a part of it.

questions.question_text: Who can become Chief Information Commissioner or Information Commissioners provided under the Right to Information, Act 2005?

options.label: A
options.option_text: Persons of eminence in public life with wide knowledge and experience in science and technology.

options.label: C
options.option_text: Member of the Legislature of Union Territory

options.label: D
options.option_text: A person connected with any political party

questions.solution_text: Under the provision of Section-12 of Right to Information, Act 2005 the Central Government I shall, by notification in the Official Gazette,constitute a body to be known as the Central S Information Commission. The Central Information Commission shall consist of the Chief Information Commissioner (CIC) and such number of Central Information Commissioners not exceeding 10 as may be deemed necessary. I Section 12(5) of the RTI Act 2005 provides that the Chief Information Commissioner and V Information Commissioners shall be persons of eminence in public life with wide knowledge and experience in law, science and technology,social service, management, journalism, mass media or administration and governance. Section 12(6) of the RTI Act 2005 provides that Chief Information Commissioner or an Information Commissioner shall not be a Member of Parliament or Member of the Legislature of any State or Union Territory as the case may be , or hold any other office of profit or connected with any political party or carrying on any business or pursuing any profession. Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

Consider the following statements regarding the Pitts India Act of 1784:
1. It allowed the Court of Directors of East India Company to manage the political affairs in India.
2. The Company’s territories in India were for the first time called the ‘British possessions in India’.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution_text: Pitt’s India Act of 1784 In a bid to rectify the defects of the Regulating Act of 1773, the British Parliament passed the Amending Act of 1781, also known as the Act of Settlement. The next important act was the Pitt’s India Act of 1784. Features of the Act It distinguished between the commercial and political functions of the Company. 3 www.visionias.in ©Vision IAS It allowed the Court of Directors to manage the commercial affairs but created a new body called the Board of Control to manage the political affairs. Thus, it established a system of double government. Hence statement 1 is not correct. It empowered the Board of Control to supervise and direct all operations of the civil and military government or revenues of the British possessions in India. Thus, the act was significant for two reasons: The Company’s territories in India were for the first time called the ‘British possessions in India’. Hence statement 2 is correct. The British Government was given supreme control over the Company’s affairs and its S administration in India.

questions.question_text: The term “Paathara (or Khoni)”, often seen in the news, refers to a:

options.label: A
options.option_text: traditional community-managed forest land system in parts of Northeast India

options.label: B
options.option_text: government scheme for afforestation under the Ministry of Environment

options.label: C
options.option_text: type of shifting cultivation practiced in hill regions of India

options.label: D
options.option_text: wildlife conservation programme for protecting endangered species

questions.solution_text: Paathara (or Khoni) refers to a traditional system of coAmmunity-managed forest lands, primarily found in parts of Northeast India such as Assam. Under this system, forest resources are collectively owned and regulated by local communities through customary laws, ensuring sustainable use and conservation. It represents an indigenous model of decentralized forest governance. The other I options are distractors: it is neither a government scheme nor a shifting cultivation practice, and it is N not a formal wildlife conservation programme. Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.question_text:
Recently, the Kumbhalgarh Wildlife Sanctuary was declared an eco- sensitive zone. In this context, consider the following statements:
1. It is located in the Aravalli hill ranges of Rajasthan.
2. It is known for being one of the few protected areas in India where the Indian wolf is found.
3. It forms part of the Gir landscape and is a key habitat for Asiatic lions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution_text: MoEFCC issued notification declaring Kumbhalgarh Wildlife Sanctuary in Aravalli mountain range as Eco-Sensitive ZOone. The Kumbhalgarh Wildlife Sanctuary is located in the Aravalli ranges of Rajasthan, making Statement 1 correct. It is also known for hosting populations of the Indian wolf, which is relatively rare in many I protected areas, thereby making Statement 2 correct. S However, Statement 3 is incorrect because the sanctuary is not part of the Gir landscape; Asiatic lions are primarily confined to Gir National Park in Gujarat. Thus, only Statements 1 and 2 are correct. I Q 1V2. B Article 39 (b) provides for the equitable distribution of material resources of the community for the common good and Article 39 (c) provides for the prevention of concentration of wealth and means of production. Article 39 (b) says that the State shall, in particular, direct its policy towards securing that the ownership and control of the material resources of the community are so distributed as best to subserve the common good. Article 39 (c) says that the State shall, in particular, direct its policy towards securing that the operation of the economic system does not result in the concentration of wealth and means of production to the common detriment. In the Golaknath Case (1967), the Supreme Court had pronounced that the Parliament cannot amend the Fundamental Rights to give effect to the Directive Principles of State Policy. The Parliament responded by bringing the 25th Amendment Act of the Constitution which inserted Article 31C in Part III. Article 31C contained two provisions. If a law is made to give effect to DPSPs in Article 39 (b) and Article 39 (c) and in the process the law violates Article 14, Article 19, or Article 31, then the law should not be declared unconstitutional and void merely on this ground. Any such law which 4 www.visionias.in ©Vision IAS contains the declaration that it is to give effect to DPSPs in Article 39 (b) and Article 39 (c) shall not be questioned in a court of law. Later, Parliament brought the 42nd Amendment Act in 1976, which extended the scope of the above first provision of Article 31C by including within its purview any law to implement any of the DPSPs specified in Part IV of the Constitution and not merely Article 39 (b) or (c). However, this extension was declared unconstitutional and void by the Supreme Court in the Minerva Mills Case (1980). These two Directive Principles under Article 39 (b) and Article 39 (c) thus have been given precedence over Fundamental Right 14 and Fundamental Right 19. S Hence option (b) is the correct answer.

With reference to the Constituent Assembly of India, consider the following statements:
1. It was a fully sovereign body that could frame any Constitution it deemed appropriate.
2. It functioned as the first Parliament of independent India after the Constitution came into force.
3. All members of the Assembly were indirectly elected.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution_text: The Constituent Assembly was constituted in November 1946 under the scheme formulated by the A Cabinet Mission Plan. The Assembly was made a fully sovereign body, which could frame any Constitution it pleased. The Assembly was empowered to abrogate or alter any law made by the British Parliament in relation to I India. Hence statement 1 is correct. N It worked as a legislative body i.e. two separate functions were assigned to the Assembly - making of a constitution for free India and enacting of ordinary laws for the country. Thus, the Assembly became the first Parliament of free India (Dominion Legislature). Hence statement 2 is correct. Whenever the AssemblyO met as the Constituent body it was chaired by Dr. Rajendra Prasad and when it met as the legislative body, it was chaired by G V Mavlankar. These two functions continued till November 26, 1949, when the task of making the Constitution was over. Although the Constituent Assembly was not directly elected by the people of India on the basis of I adult franchise, the Assembly comprised representatives of all sections of Indian society, Hindus, S Muslims, Sikhs, Parsis, Anglo–Indians, Indian Christians, SCs, STs including women of all these sections. Members from the British Indian Provinces were indirectly elected by the members of the proIvincial legislative assemblies. Members from the Princely States were nominated by the heads of those states. Therefore, saying "all members" were indirectly elected is factually inaccurate. V Hence statement 3 is not correct

NSIL, incorporated in 2019, is wholly owned Government Company under administrative control of Department of Space and is the commercial arm of Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO). About PSLV-C62 / EOS-N1 Mission: It includes the launch of EOS-N1 earth observation satellite along with 15 co-passenger satellites from domestic & international customers. EOS-N1 is designed to strengthen space-based monitoring/survellance capabilities. Hence, statements 1 and 2 are correct. It will also demonstrate KID or Kestrel Initial Technology Demonstrator from a Spanish startup. KID is a small-scale prototype of a re-entry vehicle which after launch is slated to re- 5 www.visionias.in ©Vision IAS enter the earth’s atmosphere towards splashdown in South Pacific Ocean. EOS-N1 and 14 Co-passenger satellites will be injected into a Sun Synchronous Orbit and KID Capsule into a re-entry trajectory. However, it was not related to the Gaganyaan human spaceflight programme, making Statement 3 incorrect.

With reference to judicial interpretation of the Preamble of the Constitution of India, consider the following statements:
1. In the Berubari Union Case (1960), the Supreme Court held that the Preamble is a source for interpreting the provisions of the Constitution.
2. In the LIC of India Case (1995), the Supreme Court held that the Preamble is an integral part of the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution_text: In the Berubari Union case (1960), the Supreme Court recognized the significance of the Preamble. The Supreme Court mentioned that assistance from the Preamble could be taken in the interpretation N of articles that are ambiguous or capable of more than one meaning. Hence statement 1 is correct. It also mentioned that the Preamble shows the general purposes behind several provisions in the Constitution and is thus a key to the minds of the makers of the Constitution. However, the Supreme Court specifically mentioneOd that the Preamble is not a part of the Constitution. In the LIC of India Case (1995) also, the Supreme Court again held that the Preamble is an integral part of the Constitution. Hence statement 2 is correct. I

questions.question_text: Recently, the National Investigation Agency (NIA) reported that it has achieved a conviction rate of more than 90%. In this context, under which of the following ministries does the NIA function?
questions.solution_text: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) is India’s premier central counter-terrorism investigative S agency, established under the National Investigation Agency Act, 2008 in the aftermath of the 2008 Mumbai attacks. It functions under the administrative control of the Ministry of Home Affairs. The NIA is I empowered to investigate offences related to terrorism, insurgency, and national security across Vstates without requiring special permission from state governments. Its high conviction rate reflects its specialised investigative capacity, strong legal framework, and coordination with intelligence agencies. Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.solution_text: A number of provisions in the Constitution can be amended by a simple majority of the two Houses of Parliament outside the scope of Article 368. These provisions include: Quorum in Parliament Salaries and allowances of the members of Parliament Rules of procedure in Parliament Privileges of the Parliament, its members, and its committees Use of English language in Parliament Option 3 is not correct: Those provisions of the Constitution which are related to the federal structure of the polity can be amended by a special majority of the Parliament and also with the consent of half of the state legislatures by a simple majority. The following provisions can be amended in this way: Election of the President and its manner. 6 www.visionias.in ©Vision IAS The extent of the executive power of the Union and the states. Supreme Court and high courts. Distribution of legislative powers between the Union and the state. Options 1 and 2 are correct: The majority of the provisions in the Constitution need to be amended by a special majority of the Parliament, that is, a majority of the total membership of each House and a majority of two-thirds of the members of each House present and voting. The provisions which can be amended this way include: Fundamental Rights Directive Principles of State Policy S

questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements regarding the Parliamentary form of government:
1. The ministers operate on the principle of secrecy of procedure.
2. A person who is not a member of the legislature cannot be appointed as a minister.
3. The Prime Minister is the leader of the Council of Ministers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution_text: Following are some of the features of the parliamentary form of government in India: Nominal and Real Executives: The President is the nomAinal executive (de jure executive or titular executive) while the Prime Minister is the real executive (de facto executive). Thus, the President is head of the State, while the Prime Minister is head of the government. Article 74 provides for a council of ministers headed by the Prime Minister to aid and advise the President in the exercise of I his functions. The advice so tendered is binding on the President. N Majority Party Rule: The political party which secures majority seats in the Lok Sabha forms the government. The leader of that party is appointed as the Prime Minister by the President; other ministers are appointed by the President on the advice of the prime minister. However, when no single party gets the maOjority, a coalition of parties may be invited by the President to form the government. Collective Responsibility: This is the bedrock principle of parliamentary government. The ministers are collectively responsible to the Parliament in general and to the Lok Sabha in particular I (Article 75). They act as a team, and swim and sink together. The principle of collective S responsibility implies that the Lok Sabha can remove the ministry (i.e., the council of ministers headed by the prime minister) from office by passing a vote of no confidence. Political Homogeneity: Usually members of the council of ministers belong to the same political parIty, and hence they share the same political ideology. In the case of the coalition government, the ministers are bound by consensus. V Double Membership: The ministers are members of both the legislature and the executive. This means that a person cannot be a minister without being a member of Parliament. The Constitution stipulates that a minister who is not a member of the Parliament for a period of six consecutive months ceases to be a minister. The leadership of the Prime Minister: The Prime Minister plays a leadership role in this system of government. He is the leader of the council of ministers, the leader of the Parliament, and the leader of the party in power. In these capacities, he plays a significant and highly crucial role in the functioning of the government. Hence, statement 3 is correct. Dissolution of the Lower House: The lower house of the Parliament (Lok Sabha) can be dissolved by the President on the recommendation of the Prime Minister. In other words, the prime minister can advise the President to dissolve the Lok Sabha before the expiry of its term and hold fresh elections. This means that the executive enjoys the right to get the legislature dissolved in a parliamentary system. Secrecy: The ministers operate on the principle of secrecy of procedure and cannot divulge information about their proceedings, policies, and decisions. They take the oath of secrecy before 7 www.visionias.in ©Vision IAS entering their office. The oath of secrecy to the ministers is administered by the President. Hence, statement 1 is correct. A person who is not a member of the legislature can be appointed as a minister, but must become a member of Parliament within 6 months, otherwise they cease to be a minister. Hence, statement 2 is not correct.

questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements regarding the Government of India Act of 1935:
1. It provided for the establishment of an All-India Federation consisting of provinces and princely states as units.
2. It introduced bicameralism in all the provinces.
3. It introduced dyarchy at the Centre.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution_text: The Act marked a second milestone towards a completely responsible government in India. It was a lengthy and detailed document having 321 Sections and 10 Schedules. The features of this Act were as follows: It provided for the establishment of an All-India Federation consisting of provinces and princely states as units. The Act divided the powers between the Centre and units in terms of three lists– Federal List (for Centre, with 59 items), Provincial List (for provinces, with 54 items) and the Concurrent List (for both, with 36 items). Hence statement 1 is correct. Residuary powers were given to the Viceroy. However, the federation never came into being as the princely states did not join it. It abolished dyarchy in the provinces and introduced ‘provincial autonomy’ in its place. The provinces were allowed to act as autonomous units of administration in their defined spheres. 8 www.visionias.in ©Vision IAS Moreover, the Act introduced responsible Governments in provinces, that is, the Governor was required to act with the advice of ministers responsible to the provincial legislature. This came into effect in 1937 and was discontinued in 1939. It provided for the adoption of dyarchy at the Centre. Consequently, the federal subjects were divided into reserved subjects and transferred subjects. However, this provision of the Act did not come into operation at all. It introduced bicameralism in six out of eleven provinces. Thus, the legislatures of Bengal, Bombay, Madras, Bihar, Assam and the United Provinces were made bicameral consisting of a legislative council (upper house) and a legislative assembly (lower house). However, many S restrictions were placed on them. Hence statement 2 is not correct. It further extended the principle of communal representation by providing separate electorates for depressed classes (Scheduled Castes), women and labour (workers). A It abolished the Council of India, established by the Government of India Act of 1858. The secretary of state for India was provided with a team of advisors. It extended franchise. About 10 per cent of the total population got the voting right. I It provided for the establishment of a Reserve Bank of India to control the currency and credit of the N country. It provided for the establishment of not only a Federal Public Service Commission, but also a Provincial Public Service Commission and Joint Public Service Commission for two or more provinces. O It provided for the establishment of a Federal Court, which was set up in 1937. The Act abolished dyarchy in the provinces and introduced 'provincial autonomy' in its place. Simultaneously, it provided for the adoption of dyarchy at the Centre. Consequently, the federal I subjects were divided into 'reserved subjects' and 'transferred subjects'. However, this provision of S the Act also did not come into operation. Hence, statement 3 is correct.

2. Its members holds office for a term of six years or until they attain the age of 62 years, whichever is earlier.
3. It presents its annual report to the President.
Which of the statement given above are not correct?
questions.solution_text: Statement 1 is not correct: The Constitution makes a provision for the establishment of a Joint I State Public Service Commission (JSPSC) for two or more states. While the UPSC and the SPSC Vare created directly by the Constitution, a JSPSC can be created by an act of Parliament on the request of the state legislatures concerned. Statement 2 is correct: The chairman and members of a JSPSC are appointed by the president. They hold office for a term of six years or until they attain the age of 62 years, whichever is earlier. Statement 3 is not correct: A JPSC presents its annual performance report to each of the concerned state governors. Each governor places the report before the state legislature.

questions.question_text:
With reference to the impact of a National Emergency on Fundamental Rights, consider the following statements:
1. Article 19 is automatically suspended when a National Emergency is proclaimed on the grounds of armed rebellion.
2. A presidential order suspending the enforcement of Fundamental Rights requires approval of Parliament.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution_text: Articles 358 and 359 describe the effect of a National Emergency on Fundamental Rights. Article 358 deals with the suspension of the Fundamental Rights guaranteed by Article 19, while Article 359 deals with the suspension of other Fundamental Rights (except those guaranteed by Articles 20 and 21). Article 19 containing six rights can be suspended only when the National Emergency is declared on the grounds of war or external aggression and not on the ground of armed rebellion. Article 19 is automatically suspended only when the grounds for the proclamation of emergency is either war or external aggression. This provision was not there initially and was added by the 44th constitutional amendment. Hence, statement 1 is not correct. 9 www.visionias.in ©Vision IAS Article 359 authorizes the president to suspend the right to move any court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights during a National Emergency. This means that under Article 359, the Fundamental Rights as such are not suspended, but only their enforcement. The suspension of enforcement relates to only those Fundamental Rights that are specified in the Presidential Order. Further, the suspension could be for the period during the operation of emergency or for a shorter period as mentioned in the order, and the suspension order may extend to the whole or any part of the country. Such presidential order should be laid before each House of Parliament for approval. Hence, statement 2 is correct. The 44th Amendment Act of 1978 restricted the scope of Article S359 in two ways. Firstly, the President cannot suspend the right to move the Court for the enforcement of fundamental rights guaranteed by Articles 20 to 21. In other words, the right to protection in respect of conviction for offences (Article 20) and the right to life and personal liberty (Article 21) remain enforceable even during an emergency. A Secondly, only those laws which are related to the emergency are protected from being challenged and not other laws, and the executive action taken only under such a law, is protected. I

questions.question_text:
With reference to Fundamental Duties, consider the following statements:
1. They can be implemented through appropriate legal provisions.
2. They aid the courts in examining the constitutional validity of laws.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution_text: Fundamental Duties are enforceable Nby law. The Parliament can provide for the imposition of appropriate punishment for noncompliance with any of the Fundamental Duty. Justice Verma Committee in 1999 identified legal provisions for the implementation of some of the Fundamental Duties.Hence statement 1 is correct. O Fundamental Duties help the court in determining and examining the constitutional validity of a law. In 1992, Supreme Court observed that in determining constitutionality of any law, if that law gives effect to any of the fundamental Duty then it would be considered reasonable in relation to Article 14 (equalityI before law) and Article 19 (Six freedoms) and such law would not be termed unconstitutional. Hence statement 2 is correct. S

questions.question_text:
Which of the following issues can be taken up by the National Human Rights Commission(NHRC)?
1. Issues of manual scavenging
2. Problems faced by Notified and Denotified Tribes
3. Issues related to the right to health
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
questions.solution_text: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) of India is a Statutory public body constituted under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. I The various human rights issues taken up by the Commission are as follows : V Abolition of Bonded Labour Issues Concerning Right to Food Protocols to the Convention on the Rights of the Child Abolition of Child Labour Trafficking in Women and Children Maternal Anemia and Human Rights Combating Sexual Harassment of Women at the Work Place Abolition of Manual Scavenging Dalits issues including Atrocities perpetrated on them Problems faced by Denotified and Nomadic Tribes. Rights of the Disabled Persons Issues related to Right to Health. Rights of persons affected by HIV / AIDS Hence, option (c) is the correct answer. 10 www.visionias.in ©Vision IAS

questions.question_text: Under Article 360 of the Constitution, the power to proclaim financial emergency is vested under

options.label: D
options.option_text: Comptroller and Auditor General of India

questions.solution_text: Article 360 empowers the President to proclaim a Financial Emergency if he is satisfied that a situation has arisen due to which the financial stability or credit of India or any part of its territory is threatened. The 38th Amendment Act of 1975 made the satisfaction of the President in declaring a Financial Emergency final and conclusive and not questionable in any court on any ground. But, this provision was subsequently deleted by the 44th Amendment Act of 1978 implying that the satisfaction of the President is not beyond judicial review. Hence, option (c) is correct. S

questions.question_text:
With reference to judicial pronouncements on the relationship between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles of State Policy, consider the following cases:
1. Champakam Dorairajan vs State of Madras
2. Minerva Mills vs Union of India
3. Kesavananda Bharati vs State of Kerala In which of the above cases did the Supreme Court describe the Constitution as being founded on a balance between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles?
questions.solution_text: Directive Principles were initially ignored by the Supreme Court while interpreting various socio- economic rights. It was only after the landmark verdict in the Keshavananda Bharati case in 1973 that the top court said that Directive Principles must be viewed as the guidelines by which the Fundamental Rights are realized. A Justice P. N. Bhagwati in the 1980 Minerva Mills case described that the Indian Constitution is founded on the bedrock of the balance between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles of State Policy and to give absolute primacy to one over the other is to disturb the harmony of the Constitution. I This harmony and balance is an essential feature of the basic structure of the Constitution. Hence Option 2 is correct N In the Champakam Dorairajan case (1951), the Supreme Court ruled that in case of any conflict between the Fundamental Rights and the Directive Principles, the former would prevail. Hence Option 1 is not correct O Maneka Gandhi's case is a landmark case for the implementation of Article 21. In this case, the court said that the expression personal liberty in Article 21 is of the widest amplitude and it covers a variety of rights which go to constitute the personal liberty of a person and some of them have been raised to the status of distinct fundamental rights and given additional protection under Article 19. Hence I Option 3 is not correct S Hence option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: The “LandStat” dashboard and the “Glossary of Revenue Terms”, recently seen in the news, are associated with which of the following initiatives of the Government of India?

options.label: C
options.option_text: Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme (DILRMP)

questions.solution_text: The “LandStat” dashboard and the “Glossary of Revenue Terms” are part of the Digital India Land I Records Modernization Programme (DILRMP), which aims to digitise and standardise land Vrecords across India. LandStat serves as a real-time monitoring dashboard, providing data on the progress of digitisation of land records, cadastral maps, and registration processes across states. Meanwhile, the Glossary of Revenue Terms is designed to standardise land-related terminology across different states, where variations in terms often create confusion and legal ambiguity. Together, these initiatives enhance transparency, improve accessibility of land information, reduce disputes, and strengthen governance in land administration, which is a critical reform area under the Digital India initiative. Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements :
1. Article 1 describes India as a federation of states.
2. Currently, India has 28 states and 8 union territories.
3. The names of states and union territories and their territorial extent are mentioned in the third schedule of the Constitution.
4. The consent of the concerned State Legislature is mandatory for altering its boundaries.
How many of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution_text: Article 1 describes India, that is, Bharat as a ‘Union of States’ rather than a ‘Federation of States’. This provision deals with two things: one, name of the country; and two, type of polity. Hence statement 1 is not correct. Secondly, the country is described as ‘Union’ although its Constitution is federal in structure. According to Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, the phrase ‘Union of States’ has been preferred to ‘Federation of States’ for two reasons: one, the Indian Federation is not the result of an agreement among the states like the American Federation; and two, the states have no right to secede from the federation. 11 www.visionias.in ©Vision IAS According to Article 1, the territory of India can be classified into three categories: 1. Territories of the states 2. Union territories 3. Territories that may be acquired by the Government of India at any time. The names of states and union territories and their territorial extent are mentioned in the first schedule of the Constitution. At present, there are 28 states and 8 union territories. Hence statement 2 is correct and statement 3 is not correct. Under Article 3, the Parliament can increase or diminish the area of any state or alter its boundaries. While the President must refer the bill to the concerned state legSislature for its views within a specified period, the consent is not mandatory. The Parliament is not bound by the views of the state legislature and may accept or reject them, even if the views are received in time. Hence, statement 4 is not correct. A

questions.question_text: Swadesh Darshan 2.0, PRASHAD, and SASCI are initiatives of which of the following ministries?
questions.solution_text: Schemes like Swadesh Darshan 2.0, PRASHAD (Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual Augmentation Drive), and SASCI (Special AssistanIce to States for Capital Investment – tourism- related components) are all associated with the Ministry of Tourism. These initiatives aim to N promote tourism infrastructure, develop spiritual and heritage destinations, and enhance the overall tourism ecosystem in India. They play a key role in boosting regional economies, employment, and cultural preservation. Hence, option (a) is the correct answer. O

questions.question_text:
With reference to Lepidagathis konkanensis, recently seen in the news, consider the following statements:
1. It is a newly identified plant species endemic to the Konkan region of India.
2. It belongs to the grass family (Poaceae) and is primarily found in desert ecosystems.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution_text: Lepidagathis konkanensis is a recently discovered plant species endemic to the Konkan region of India, making Statement I correct. It belongs to the family Acanthaceae, not Poaceae, and is typically found in lateritic plateaus and rocky habitats rather than desert ecosystems, which makes I Statement II not correct. S The discovery of such endemic species highlights the rich biodiversity of the Western Ghats and the need for conservation of fragile ecosystems like lateritic plateaus. I

questions.question_text:
With reference to the Directive Principles of State Policy, consider the following statements:
1. Promoting cottage industries on an individual or cooperative basis in rural areas.
2. Public assistance in cases of old age, sickness, and disablement, and right to work.
3. Promoting the educational and economic interests of SCs, STs, and other weaker sections.
Which of the above are based on Gandhian ideology?
questions.solution_text: The Constitution does not contain any classification of Directive Principles. However, on the basis of Vtheir content and direction, they can be classified into three broad categories as socialistic, Gandhian, and liberal-intellectual. Gandhian Principles are based on Gandhian ideology. They represent the program of reconstruction enunciated by Gandhi during the national movement. In order to fulfill the dreams of Gandhi, some of his ideas were included as Directive Principles. To organize village panchayats and endow them with necessary powers and authority to enable them to function as units of self-government (Article 40). To promote cottage industries on an individual or cooperative basis in rural areas (Article 43). Hence, statement 1 is correct To promote voluntary formation, autonomous functioning, democratic control, and professional management of cooperative societies (Article 43B). To promote the educational and economic interests of SCs, STs, and other weaker sections of the society and to protect them from social injustice and exploitation (Article 46). Hence, statement 3 is correct To prohibit the consumption of intoxicating drinks and drugs which are injurious to health (Article 47). 12 www.visionias.in ©Vision IAS To prohibit the slaughter of cows, calves, and other milch and draught cattle and to improve their breeds (Article 48). To secure the right to work, to education, and to public assistance in cases of unemployment, old age, sickness, and disablement (Article 41). This is a socialist directive principle. Hence, statement 2 is not correct Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.question_text:
With reference to the International Spice Conference (ISC) 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It is organised by the Spices Board of India.
2. It serves as a global platform for stakeholders involved in spice trade, sustainability, and value addition.
3. It is conducted under the aegis of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution_text: The International Spice Conference (ISC) is a major global event organised by the Spices Board of India, which functions under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, not the Ministry of S Agriculture. It brings together global stakeholders including spice producers, exporters, researchers, and policymakers to discuss issues such as sustainability, quality standards, traceability, and value addition in the spice sector. Therefore, Statements 1 and 2 are correct, while Statement 3 is incorrect. A

questions.question_text: Which of the following is essentially not a feature of a federal polity?
questions.solution_text: Dual citizenship is not an essential feature of a federal polity. In some federal countries like India, there is single citizenship. Essential features oIf a federal polity: Two set of polities- at the national leNvel and at the regional level Written constitution Rigid constitution Supremacy of ConstituOtion Independent judiciary Bicameral legislature Division of powers between the national and regional governments. I Hence option (a) is the correct answer. S

questions.question_text:
Which of the following situations can be considered 'proper' for the imposition of President’s Rule in a state?
1. Maladministration in the state
2. A government is deliberately acting against the Constitution.
3. A constitutional direction of the Central government is disregarded by the state government
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.solution_text: Based on the report of the Sarkaria Commission on Centre–State Relations (1988), the Supreme Court in Bommai case (1994) enlisted the situations where the exercise of power under Article 356 I could be proper or improper. V The imposition of President’s Rule in a state would be proper in the following situations: Where after general elections to the assembly, no party secures a majority, that is, ‘Hung Assembly’. Where the party having a majority in the assembly declines to form a ministry and the governor cannot find a coalition ministry commanding a majority in the assembly. Where a ministry resigns after its defeat in the assembly and no other party is willing or able to form a ministry commanding a majority in the assembly. Where a constitutional direction of the Central government is disregarded by the state government. Internal subversion where, for example, a government is deliberately acting against the Constitution and the law or is fomenting a violent revolt. Physical breakdown where the government wilfully refuses to discharge its constitutional obligations endangering the security of the state. The imposition of President’s Rule in a state would be improper under the following situations: 13 www.visionias.in ©Vision IAS Where a ministry resigns or is dismissed on losing majority support in the assembly and the governor recommends imposition of President’s Rule without probing the possibility of forming an alternative ministry. Where the governor makes his own assessment of the support of a ministry in the assembly and recommends imposition of President’s Rule without allowing the ministry to prove its majority on the floor of the Assembly. Where the ruling party enjoying majority support in the assembly has suffered a massive defeat in the general elections to the Lok Sabha such as in 1977 and 1980. Internal disturbances not amounting to internal subversion or physical breakdown S Maladministration in the state or allegations of corruption against the ministry or stringent financial exigencies of the state. Where the state government is not given prior warning to rectify itself except in case of extreme A urgency leading to disastrous consequences. Where the power is used to sort out intra-party problems of the ruling party, or for a purpose extraneous or irrelevant to the one for which it has been conferred by the Constitution. I N

questions.question_text:
Which of the following is/are the functions of a constitution in a democratic country?
1. It checks the power of the government.
2. It acts as an instrument of political self- determination.
3. It guarantees absolute and unrestricted rights to citizens.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.solution_text: Constitution as Means of Democratic Transformation: It is widely agreed that one reason for having constitutions is the need to restrict the exercise of power. Experience of state power the world over shows that most states are prone to harming the interests of at least some individuals and groups. If so, we need toO draw the rules of the game in such a way that this tendency of states is continuously checked. Constitutions provide these basic rules and therefore, prevent states from turning tyrannical. Hence statement 1 is correct. Moreover, for a hitherto colonized people, constitutions announce and embody the first real I exercise of political self-determination. Hence statement 2 is correct. S In most democratic countries, including India, the rights guaranteed to citizens are not absolute or unrestricted. They are subject to reasonable restrictions in the interest of public order, national security, morality, and the sovereignty and integrity of the nation. For instance, the Right to FreIedom of Speech does not allow one to incite violence or defame others. Hence statement 3 is not correct. V

questions.question_text:
With reference to State Election Commission, consider the following statements:
1. It has been empowered to conduct elections to panchayats through 73rd Constitutional amendment.
2. The functions of delimitation, reservation and rotation of Panchayats seats is vested in State Election Commission.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution_text: The State Election Commission in India is constituted under Article 243K of the Constitution, which deals with elections to Panchayats, and Article 243ZA, which covers elections to Municipalities. Statement 1 is correct: State Election Commissions is entrusted to conduct elections to Panchayats through 73rd and urban local bodies through 74th Constitutional amendment acts. Statement 2 is correct: The functions of delimitation, reservation and rotation of Panchayats seats is vested in State Election Commission. As per the recommendations of National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution (NCRWC), the functions of delimitation, reservation and rotation of seats should be vested in a Delimitation Commission and not in the State Election Commission. Hence option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.question_text:
Consider the following words in the Preamble of the Indian Constitution:
1. Dignity
2. Unity
3. Secular
Which of the above words were introduced by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976?
questions.solution_text: The Preamble of the Indian Constitution can be amended provided that no amendment is done to the basic features of the Constitution enshrined in the Preamble. 14 www.visionias.in ©Vision IAS The Preamble has been amended only once by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act in 1976. By this amendment, three words were added to the Preamble which are Socialist, Secular, and Integrity. Hence option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements:
1. Chairpersons of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) and State Human Rights Commission (SHRC) are appointed by the President of India.
2. Only the President of India can remove the chairpersons of NHRC and SHRC.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution_text: The Protection of Human Rights Act of 1993 provides for the creation of the National Human Rights Commission and State Human Rights Commission at the state level. A State Human Rights Commission can inquire into violation of human rights only in respect of subjects mentioned in the State List and the Concurrent List of the Constitution. However, if any such case is already being inquired into by the National Human Rights S Commission or any other Statutory Commission, then the State Human Rights Commission does not inquire into that case. The chairperson and members of SHRC are appointed by the Governor. Whereas, in the case of A NHRC, they are appointed by the President of India. Hence, statement 1 is not correct. Although the chairperson and members of an SHRC are appointed by the governor, they can be removed only by the President. Hence statement 2 is correct. I N

questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements.
1. Revocation of President’s rule in a state requires parliamentary approval.
2. 44th Amendment Act of 1978 restrained the power of Parliament to extend a proclamation of President’s Rule.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution_text: Statement 1 is not correct: A proclamation of President’s Rule may be revoked by the President at any time by a subsequent proclamation. Such a proclamation does not require the parliamentary approval. O Statement 2 is correct: The 44th Amendment Act of 1978 introduced a new provision to put restraint on the power of Parliament to extend a proclamation of President’s Rule beyond one year. Thus, it provided that, beyond one year, the President’s Rule can be extended by six months at a time only when the following two conditions are fulfilled: 1. a proclamation of National Emergency I should be in operation in the whole of India, or in the whole or any part of the state; and 2. the ElectionS Commission must certify that the general elections to the legislative assembly of the concerned state cannot be held on account of difficulties.

questions.question_text:
With reference to Sagar Island, consider the following statements:
1. It is located at the mouth of the Hooghly River in the Bay of Bengal.
2. It is known for hosting the annual Gangasagar Mela, one of the largest religious gatherings in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution_text: Re I cently, the West Bengal Chief Minister laid the foundation stone of a 5-km bridge over the VMuriganga River to connect Sagar Island with the mainland. Sagar Island is situated at the confluence of the Hooghly River and the Bay of Bengal, making Statement 1 correct. It is also famous for hosting the annual Gangasagar Mela, a major religious congregation attracting lakhs of pilgrims, thereby making Statement 2 correct. The island was in the news in January 2026 due to extensive arrangements for the Gangasagar Mela, including improved infrastructure, crowd management systems, and disaster preparedness measures.

questions.question_text: A new state can be formed by uniting two or more states through a bill passed by:

options.label: B
options.option_text: A simple majority in state assemblies of both the states

options.label: C
options.option_text: A Special majority in the parliament and ratification by half of the states

questions.solution_text: Article 3 authorizes the Parliament to: form a new state by separation of territory from any state or by uniting two or more states or parts of states or by uniting any territory to a part of any state; increase the area of any state; diminish the area of any state; alter the boundaries of any state; and alter the name of any state. A bill contemplating the changes under Article 3 has to satisfy two conditions: 15 www.visionias.in ©Vision IAS such a bill can be introduced in the Parliament only with the prior recommendation of the President; before recommending the bill, the President has to refer the same to the state legislature concerned for expressing its views within a specified period. The President is not bound by the views of the state legislature and may either accept or reject them, even if the views are received in time. Moreover, the Constitution (Article 4) itself declares that laws made for admission or establishment of new states (under Article 2) and formation of new states and alteration of areas, boundaries or names of existing states (under Article 3) are not to be considered as amendments of the Constitution under Article 368. This means that such laws can S be passed by a simple majority and by the ordinary legislative process. Hence, option (a) is the correct answer. A

questions.question_text:
Consider the following pairs: Commission/B Falls under ody
1. National : Ministry of Social Commission Justice & for Minorities Empowerment
2. National : Ministry of Women Commission and Child for Women Development
3. National : Ministry of Tribal Commission Affairs for STs

questions.solution_text: National Commission for Minorities falls under the Minorities Ministry of Minority Affairs. National Commission for Women falls under the Ministry of Women and Child Development. National Commission for STs falls under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs. I Hence, only pairs 2 and 3 are correctly matched. N

questions.question_text: Which of the following institutions recently released the report titled “Achieving Efficiencies in MSME Sector through Convergence of Schemes”?

options.label: B
options.option_text: Small Industries ZDevelopment Bank of InZdia

options.label: D
options.option_text: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises

questions.solution_text: The report titled “Achieving Efficiencies in MSME Sector through Convergence of Schemes” was released by NITI Aayog. It focuses on improving the effectiveness of various government schemes O targeted at the MSME sector by promoting convergence, reducing duplication, and enhancing coordination among different ministries and institutions. The objective is to streamline policy implementation and ensure better outcomes for micro, small, and medium enterprises, which are crucial for employment generation and economic growth in India. Hence, option (c) is the correct I answer. S

questions.question_text: The term 'Plasticosis', recently seen in environmental studies, refers to:

options.label: A
options.option_text: the process of turning plastic waste into paving tiles.

options.label: B
options.option_text: a specialized bacteria that can digest plastic in the deep ocean.

options.label: C
options.option_text: the accumulation of microplastics in the leaves of agricultural crops.

options.label: D
options.option_text: a fibrotic disease in seabirds caused by the ingestion of small plastic fragments.

questions.solution_text: Plasticosis is a newly identified disease where ingested microplastics cause chronic inflammation and scarring in the digestive tracts (specifically the proventriculus or first chamber of the stomach) I of seabirds, such as the flesh-footed shearwater. V Tiny shards of plastic become lodged in the stomach tissue, leading to scar tissue formation (fibrosis) that replaces healthy tissue, impairing digestion, reducing nutrient absorption, and stunting growth. The term was coined by researchers to differentiate this condition, caused solely by plastic, from other fibrotic diseases caused by inorganic materials, such as silicosis (silica) or asbestosis (asbestos). Impact: While initially identified in seabirds, it indicates a broader, dangerous impact of plastic pollution on wildlife and potentially other organisms. Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements with respect to the National Commission on Minorities:
1. It has been established by an act of Parliament.
2. It has all the powers of a civil court while trying a suit related to complaints regarding deprivation of rights of minorities.
3. It is required to make periodical reports to President on matters pertaining to minorities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution_text: The Union Government set up the National Commission for Minorities (NCM) under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992. Neither the Act nor the Constitution define the term minorities but under Section 2(c) of the Act, Central Government notified six religious communities - Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains and Zoroastrians as minorities communities. Hence statement 1 is correct. 16 www.visionias.in ©Vision IAS As per the NCM Act 1992, the Commission consists of a Chairperson, a Vice - Chairperson, five members i.e. total of 7 persons to be nominated by the Central Government from amongst persons of eminence, ability and integrity. The Commission is required to perform following functions: evaluation of the progress of the development of minorities under the Union and States; making recommendations for the effective implementation of safeguards for the protection of the interests of minorities by the Central Government or the State Governments; conducting studies, research and analysis on the issues relating to socio-economic and educational development of minorities; S making periodical or special reports to the Central Government on any matter pertaining to minorities and in particular the difficulties confronted by them etc. Hence statement 3 is not correct. A The Commission have all the powers of a civil court trying a suit while evaluating the progress of minorities, monitoring the working of the safeguards provided in the Constitution, and looking into specific complaints of discrimination against minorities. Hence statement 2 is correct. I N

questions.question_text: Who among the following first put forward the idea of the Constituent Assembly for India?
questions.solution_text: It was in 1934 that the idea of a Constituent Assembly for India was put forward for the first time by M. N. Roy, a pioneer of communist movement in India and an advocate of radical democratism. In 1935, the Indian National Congress (INC), for the first time, officially demanded a Constituent Assembly to frame the COonstitution of India. In 1938, Jawaharlal Nehru, on behalf the INC declared that ‘the Constitution of free India must be framed, without outside interference, by a Constituent Assembly elected on the basis of adult franchise’. Hence, option (d) is the correct answer. I

questions.question_text:
In the context Constituent Assembly of India, consider the following pairs: Committee Chairman
1. Union Powers : Jawaharlal Nehru Committee
2. Steering : Sardar Patel Committee
3. Provincial : Dr. Rajendra Prasad Constitution Committee
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
questions.solution_text: The Constituent Assembly appointed a number of committees to deal with different tasks of S constitution-making. Out of these, eight were major committees and the others were minor committees. Union Powers Committee - Jawaharlal Nehru. Hence pair 1 is correctly matched. I Union Constitution Committee - Jawaharlal Nehru V Provincial Constitution Committee - Sardar Patel. Hence pair 3 is not correctly matched. Drafting Committee - Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribal and Excluded Areas - Sardar Patel. This committee had the following five sub-committees: Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee - J.B. Kripalani Minorities Sub-Committee - H.C. Mukherjee North-East Frontier Tribal Areas and Assam Excluded & Partially Excluded Areas Sub- Committee -Gopinath Bardoloi Excluded and Partially Excluded Areas (other than those in Assam) Sub-Committee - A.V. Thakkar North-West Frontier Tribal Areas Sub-Committee8a Rules of Procedure Committee - Dr. Rajendra Prasad States Committee (Committee for Negotiating with States) - Jawaharlal Nehru. 17 www.visionias.in ©Vision IAS Steering Committee - Dr. Rajendra Prasad. Hence pair 2 is not correctly matched. Hence option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: Which of the following best describes the concept of Constitutionalism?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It is an ideology which promotes supremacy of a written Constitution.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It means the Constitution is necessary in a democratic country.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It denotes the principle that the government derives its authority from a body of fundamental law and is limited by it.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It means that the Constitution must provide certain inalienable rights to the citizens.

questions.solution_text: Constitutionalism: Constitutionalism is a concept that means the government derives its authority from a fundamental body of law and is legally limited in its powers by the same. Hence option (c) is the correct answer. It does not have any direct relation to the written or unwritten constitution or the political system of a country. S It involves the principles and practices that ensure the government's authority is derived from and limited by a body of fundamental laws laid out in the Constitution. Constitutionalism promotes the rule of law, the separaAtion of powers, the protection of individual rights, and adherence to legal constraints, fostering a system where government actions are governed by established legal norms and principles. It reflects the idea that governmental powers Ishould be structured and controlled within a framework defined by the Constitution to prevent arbitrary rule and protect the rights of citizens. N

questions.question_text:
How many of the following were members of the Interim Government formed in 1946?
1. Liaquat Ali Khan
2. Sardar Patel
3. Dr. John Mathai
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.solution_text: The Interim Government of India was formed in 1946. It also included the Viceroy and Commander-in-Chief of Britain and other members from All-India Muslim League. O The government was formed to assist the switch of British India to India and Pakistan. Its members included: Jawaharlal Nehru as Vice President Sardar Patel I Dr. RSajdendra Prasad Dr. John Mathai Jagjivan Ram I Sardar Baldev Singh VC. Rajagopalachari Liaquat Ali Khan Hence. Option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements regarding the differences between the Indian and British polity:
1. The Indian system is based on the doctrine of the sovereignty of Parliament, while Parliament is not supreme in Britain.
2. In Britain, the Prime Minister must be a member of the lower house of Parliament (House of Commons).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution_text: The parliamentary system of government in India is largely based on the British parliamentary system. However, it never became a replica of the British system and differs in the following respects: India has a republican system in place of the British monarchical system. In other words, the Head of the State in India (that is, President) is elected, while the Head of the State in Britain (that is, King or Queen) enjoys a hereditary position. The British system is based on the doctrine of the sovereignty of Parliament, while the Parliament is not supreme in India and enjoys limited and restricted powers due to a written Constitution, the federal system, judicial review, and fundamental rights. Hence statement 1 is not correct. In Britain, the prime minister should be a member of the Lower House (House of Commons) of the Parliament. In India, the prime minister may be a member of any of the two Houses of 18 www.visionias.in ©Vision IAS Parliament. Usually, the members of Parliament alone are appointed as ministers in Britain. In India, a person who is not a member of Parliament can also be appointed as minister, but for a maximum period of six months. Britain has the system of legal responsibility of the minister while India has no such system. Unlike in Britain, the ministers in India are not required to countersign the official acts of the Head of the State. ‘Shadow cabinet’ is an unique institution of the British cabinet system. It is formed by the opposition party to balance the ruling cabinet and to prepare its members for future ministerial S office. There is no such institution in India. Britain: By convention, the Prime Minister must be a member of the lower house (House of Commons). A India: The Prime Minister can be a member of either the Lok Sabha (Lower House) or the Rajya Sabha (Upper House). For example, Indira Gandhi, H.D. Deve Gowda, and Dr. Manmohan Singh were members of the Rajya Sabha during their tenures as Prime I Minister. Hence statement 2 is correct. N

questions.solution_text: The Overseas Citizens of India (OCI) cards provide long-term visa-free travel and stay in India and gives the cardholders a host of privileges normally not given to a foreign national. Hence statement 1 is correct. O With the new notification, an OCI cardholder will now have to take special permission to undertake research work. The Notification also permits OCI cardholders eligible for appearing in all-India entrance tests such as NEET for medical courses, JEE — both Main and Advanced — for I engineering or any other tests. However, this will only be against any NRI or supernumerary seat that is oSver and above the sanctioned intake approved by the appropriate authority and government, from time to time. questions.question_text:
With reference to Directive Principles of State Policy, consider the following:
1. To provide free legal aid to the poor.
2. To protect and improve the environment and to safeguard forests and wildlife.
3. To minimise inequalities in income, status, facilities, and opportunities.
Which of the above were added through constitutional amendments?
questions.solution_text: The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 added four new Directive Principles to the original list. They are to secure opportunities for the healthy development of children under Article 39, to promote equal justice and to provide free legal aid to the poor under Article 39A, to take steps to secure the participation of workers in the management of industries under Article 43A, and to protect and improve the environment and to safeguard forests and wildlife under Article 48A. Hence statement 1 and 2 are correct. The 44th Amendment Act of 1978 added one more Directive Principle, which requires the State to minimize inequalities in income, status, facilities, and opportunities under Article 38. Hence statement 3 is correct. The 86th Amendment Act of 2002 changed the subject matter of Article 45 and made elementary education a fundamental right under Article 21A. The amended directive requires the State to provide early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years. The 97th Amendment Act of 2011 added a new Directive Principle relating to cooperative societies. It requires the State to promote voluntary formation, autonomous functioning, democratic control, and professional management of cooperative societies under Article 43B. 19 www.visionias.in ©Vision IAS Raising the level of nutrition and the standard of living of people and improving public health under Article 47 has been there since the adoption of the Constitution and not added by way of amendment. Hence option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.question_text:
Who among the following are not members of the Selection Committee for the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and Election Commissioners (ECs) in India?
1. Prime Minister of India
2. Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha
3. Chief Justice of India
4. Leader of Opposition of the Rajya Sabha
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.solution_text: As per the the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, the Selection Committee for the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and Election Commissioners (ECs) in India consists of three members: the Prime Minister (Chairperson), the Leader of Opposition (LoP) in the Lok Sabha, and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister. S In the Anoop Baranwal Case, 2023, the Supreme Court ruled that a panel of the Prime Minister, LoP, and CJI would select CEC and ECs until Parliament passed a law. This committee recommends names to the President of India for the appointment of the CEC and A other Election Commissioners, with decisions made by a majority vote. This structure replaced the previous arrangement which included the Chief Justice of India. Hence options 3 and 4 are correct. I N

questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements:
1. Since Independence, India has had a national emergency only once.
2. Since Independence, India has never faced a financial emergency.
3. President’s Rule was imposed for the first time in Punjab in 1951.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution_text: Article 352 of the Constitution details about National emergency in India. Such an emergency was declared in India in the 1962 war (China war), 1971 war (Pakistan war), and 1975 internal disturbance (declared by Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed). Hence, statement 1 is not correct. Article 360 of the IndianO Constitution empowers the President to invoke a financial emergency. The Financial emergency has never been proclaimed in India since independence, thanks to various fiscal and monetary policy measures even during the time of distress. Hence, statement 2 is correct. I Article 356 and Article 365 detail about State emergencies. The President's rule was first imposedS in India in Punjab on June 20, 1951. This was done in order to control the intense infighting within the Punjab Congress. The President’s rule, which was supposed to be enforced in the rarest of the rare situations, has since been used even for the Central Government to have its waIy in the states. Hence, statement 3 is correct. V

questions.question_text:
In the context of direct democracy, consider the following pairs: Device Description
1. Referendum : Procedure whereby proposed legislation is referred to the electorate for settlement by their direct votes
2. Recall : Method of obtaining the opinion of people on any issue of public importance
3. Plebiscite : Method by means of which the voters can remove a representative before the expiry of his term
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
questions.solution_text: Democracy is of two types–direct and indirect. In direct democracy, the people exercise their supreme power directly as is the case in Switzerland. There are four devices of direct democracy, namely, Referendum, Initiative, Recall and Plebiscite. In indirect democracy, on the other hand, the representatives elected by the people exercise the supreme power and thus carry on the government and make the laws. This type of democracy, also known as representative democracy. Referendum is a procedure whereby proposed legislation is referred to the electorate for settlement by their direct votes. Hence pair 1 is correctly matched. Initiative is a method by means of which the people can propose a bill to the legislature for enactment. Recall is a method by means of which the voters can remove a representative or an officer before the expiry of his term, when he fails to discharge his duties properly. Hence pair 2 is not correctly matched. Plebiscite is a method of obtaining the opinion of people on any issue of public importance. It is generally used to solve the territorial disputes. Hence pair 3 is not correctly matched. 20 www.visionias.in ©Vision IAS
