questions.question_text:
With reference to the Central Vigilance Commission, consider the following statements:
1. It is a constitutional body.
2. Its Chairman and members are appointed by the President.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution_text: The Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) is the main agency for preventing corruption in the Central government. It was established in 1964 by an executive resolution of the Central A government. Its establishment was recommended by the Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption (1962–64). Thus, originally the CVC was neither a constitutional body nor a statutory body. Later, in 2003, the Parliament enacted a law conferring statutory status on the CVC. Hence, I statement 1 is not correct. N The CVC is a multi-member body consisting of a Central Vigilance Commissioner (chairperson) and not more than two vigilance commissioners. They are appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal on the recommendation of a three-member committee consisting of the prime minister as its head, the Union minister of home affairs and the Leader of the Opposition in O the Lok Sabha. They hold office for a term of four years or until they attain the age of sixty five years, whichever is earlier. After their tenure, they are not eligible for further employment under the Central or a state government. Hence, statement 2 is correct. I

questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements regarding ' State Public Service Commission' :
1. One-half of the members of the commission should be persons from SC/ST and OBCs.
2. Members of the SPSC can be removed by the Governor of the respective state.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution_text: A StateS Public Service Commission consists of a chairman and other members appointed by the governor of the state. The Constitution does not specify the strength of the Commission but has left the matter to the discretion of the Governor. Further, no qualifications are prescribed for the commission's membership except that one-half of the members of the commission should be such I persons who have held office for at least ten years either under the government of India or under the V Government of a state. The Constitution also authorizes the governor to determine the conditions of service of the chairman and members of the Commission. Hence statement 1 is not correct. Although the chairman and members of an SPSC are appointed by the governor, they can be removed only by the President (and not by the governor). The President can remove them on the same grounds and in the same manner as he can remove a chairman or a member of the UPSC. Hence statement 2 is not correct.

questions.question_text:
With reference to the Fundamental Rights of members of the armed forces, consider the following statements:
1. Parliament can restrict but cannot abrogate their Fundamental Rights.
2. The term ‘members of the armed forces’ also includes employees such as mechanics and cooks who are non- combatants.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution_text: Article 33 empowers the Parliament to restrict or 'abrogate' the fundamental rights of the members of armed forces, para-military forces, police forces, intelligence agencies, and analogous forces. Hence statement 1 is not correct. The objective of this provision is to ensure the proper discharge of their duties and the maintenance of discipline among them. The power to make laws under Article 33 is conferred only on Parliament and not on state legislatures. Any such law made by Parliament cannot be challenged in any court on the ground of contravention of any of the fundamental rights. 21 www.visionias.in ©Vision IAS Accordingly, the Parliament has enacted the Army Act (1950), the Navy Act (1950), the Air Force Act (1950), the Police Forces (Restriction of Rights) Act, 1966, the Border Security Force Act, etc. These impose restrictions on their freedom of speech, right to form associations, right to be members of trade unions or political associations, right to communicate with the press, right to attend public meetings or demonstrations, etc. The expression members of the armed forces’ also covers such employees of the armed forces as barbers, carpenters, mechanics, cooks, chowkidars, bootmakers, tailors who are non-combatants. Hence, statement 2 is correct. A parliamentary law enacted under Article 33 can also exclude the court-martial (tribunals S established under the military law) from the writ jurisdiction of the Supreme Court and the high courts, so far as the enforcement of Fundamental Rights is concerned. A

questions.question_text:
With reference to the Right to Freedom of Religion, consider the following statements:
1. It covers only religious beliefs and not religious practices or rituals.
2. No religious instruction shall be provided in any educational institution administered by the State.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution_text: Article 25 says that all persons are equally entitled to freedom of conscience and the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate religion. The implications of these are: Freedom of conscience means the inner freedom of an individual to I mold his relation with God or Creatures in whatever way he desires. The right to profess means the declaration of one’s religious beliefs and faith openly and freely. The right to practice refers to the N performance of religious worship, rituals, ceremonies, and exhibition of beliefs and ideas. The right to propagate refers to the transmission and dissemination of one’s religious beliefs to others or exposition of the tenets of one’s religion, but it does not include a right to convert another person to one’s own religion. O From the above, it is clear that Article 25 covers not only religious beliefs but also religious practices and these rights are available to all persons, including citizens as well as non-citizens. Hence, statement 1 is not correct. I However, these rights are subject to public order, morality, health, and other provisions relating to fundamental rights. Further, the State is permitted to regulate or restrict any economic, financial, S political, or other secular activity associated with religious practice and to provide for social welfare and reform or throw open Hindu religious institutions of a public character to all classes and sections of Hindus. I Under Article 28, no religious instruction shall be provided in any educational institution wholly Vmaintained out of State funds. However, this provision does not apply to an educational institution administered by the State but established under any endowment or trust which requires imparting of religious instruction in such institution. Hence statement 2 is not correct. Further, no person attending any educational institution recognized by the State or receiving aid out of State funds shall be required to attend any religious instruction or worship in that institution without his consent. Thus, Article 28 distinguishes between four types of educational institutions: institutions wholly maintained by the State, institutions administered by the State but established under any endowment or trust, institutions recognized by the State, and institutions receiving aid from the State. In institutions wholly maintained by the State, religious instruction is completely prohibited, while in institutions administered by the State but established under any endowment or trust, religious instruction is permitted. In institutions recognized by the State and those receiving aid from the State, religious instruction is permitted on a voluntary basis.

With reference to the settlement of a border dispute without ceding any Indian territory, consider the following statements:
1. It can be effected through a law passed by the Parliament with a simple majority.
2. It does not require a constitutional amendment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution_text: The Supreme Court in 1969 ruled that settlement of a boundary dispute between India and another country does not require a constitutional amendment. It can be done by executive action as it does I not involve cession of Indian territory to a foreign country. Hence statement 1 not correct but N statement 2 is correct. While the decision of the Central Government to cede part of a territory known as Berubari Union (West Bengal) to Pakistan led to political agitation and controversy and thereby necessitated the Presidential reference. O The Supreme Court held that the power of Parliament to diminish the area of a state (under Article 3) does not cover cession of Indian territory to a foreign country. Hence, Indian territory can be ceded to a foreign state only by amending the Constitution under Article 368. Consequently, the 9th I Constitutional Amendment Act (1960) was enacted to transfer the said territory to Pakistan. S

questions.question_text: In the context of the historical underpinnings of the Indian constitution, which of the following Acts introduced ordinances for the first time?
questions.solution_text: After the great revolt of 1857, the British Government felt the necessity of seeking the cooperation of the Indians in the administration of their country. In pursuance of this policy of association, three actIs were enacted by the British Parliament in 1861, 1892 and 1909. The Indian Councils Act of 1861 is an important landmark in the constitutional and political history of India. V The features of this Act were as follows It made the beginning of the representative institutions by associating Indians with the law- making process. It, thus, provided that the Viceroy should nominate some Indians as non-official members of his expanded council. In 1862, Lord Canning, the then Viceroy, nominated three Indians to his legislative council–the Raja of Benaras, the Maharaja of Patiala and Sir Dinkar Rao. It initiated the process of decentralization by restoring the legislative powers to the Bombay and Madras Presidencies. It also provided for the establishment of new legislative councils for Bengal, North-Western Provinces and Punjab, which were established in 1862, 1886 and 1897, respectively. It empowered the Viceroy to make rules and orders for the more convenient transaction of business in the council. It also gave recognition to the ‘portfolio’ system, introduced by Lord Canning in 1859. Under this, a member of the Viceroy’s council was made in-charge of one or more departments of the Government and was authorised to issue final orders on behalf of the council on matters of his department(s). 23 www.visionias.in ©Vision IAS It empowered the Viceroy to issue ordinances without the concurrence of the legislative council, during an emergency. Hence option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: Which of the following has defined what constitutes the ‘Doctrine of Basic Structure’?
questions.solution_text: The question whether the Parliament can amend Fundamental Rights under Article 368 came for consideration of the Supreme Court within a year of the Constitution coming into force. Through a series of judgments like Shankari Prasad (1951) and Golaknath (1967) the Supreme Court opined on this. In the Golak Nath case, the Supreme Court ruled that the Fundamental Rights are given a S ‘transcendental and immutable’ position and hence, the Parliament cannot abridge or take away any of these rights. The Parliament reacted to the Supreme Court’s judgment in the Golak Nath case (1967) by enacting A the 24th Amendment Act (1971). This Act amended Articles 13 and 368. It declared that the Parliament has the power to abridge or take away any of the Fundamental Rights under Article 368 and such an act will not be a law under the meaning of Article 13. I However, in the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973), the Supreme Court overruled its judgment in the N Golak Nath case (1967). It upheld the validity of the 24th Amendment Act (1971) and stated that Parliament can abridge or take away any of the Fundamental Rights. At the same time, it laid down a new doctrine of the ‘basic structure’ (or ‘basic features’) of the Constitution. It ruled that the constituent power of Parliament under Article 368 does not enable it to alter the ‘basic structure’ of O the Constitution. This means that the Parliament cannot abridge or take away a Fundamental Right that forms a part of the ‘basic structure’ of the Constitution. The present position is that the Parliament under Article 368 can amend any part of the Constitution includIing the Fundamental Rights but without affecting the ‘basic structure’ of the ConSstitution. However, the Supreme Court has yet to define or clarify what constitutes the ‘basic structure’ of the Constitution. Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements regarding the reorganization of the states:
1. An Indian territory can be ceded to a foreign country by a constitutional amendment.
2. A boundary dispute settlement between India and another country does not require a constitutional amendment.
Which of the statements given above is/are not correct?
questions.solution_text: ThIe Supreme Court held that the power of Parliament to diminish the area of a state (under Article 3) does not cover the cession of Indian territory to a foreign country. Hence, Indian territory can V be ceded to a foreign state only by amending the Constitution under Article 368. Consequently, the 9th Constitutional Amendment Act (1960) was enacted to transfer the said territory to Pakistan. Hence, statement 1 is correct. On the other hand, the Supreme Court in 1969 ruled that, the settlement of a boundary dispute between India and another country does not require a constitutional amendment. It can be done by executive action as it does not involve the cession of Indian territory to a foreign country. Hence, statement 2 is correct.

questions.question_text:
With reference to the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities, consider the following statements:
1. It was constituted under Article 350-B of the Indian Constitution.
2. It can investigate all matters relating to the safeguards provided for both linguistic and religious minorities under the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution_text: Originally, the Constitution of India did not make any provision with respect to the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities. Later, the States Reorganisation Commission (1953-55) made a recommendation in this regard. Accordingly, the Seventh Constitutional Amendment Act of 1956 inserted a new Article 350-B in Part XVII of the Constitution.Hence, statement 1 is correct. This article contains the following provisions: 1. There should be a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities. He is to be appointed by the President of India. 24 www.visionias.in ©Vision IAS 2. It would be the duty of the Special Officer to investigate all matters only relating to the safeguards provided for linguistic minorities under the Constitution. He would report to the President upon those matters at such intervals as the President may direct. The President should place all such reports before each House of Parliament and send to the governments of the states concerned. Hence, statement 2 is not correct.

questions.question_text:
The Indian Army recently conducted Exercise ‘Sanjha Shakti’, a joint Military– Civil Fusion exercise. In this context, consider the following statements:
1. The exercise aims to enhance coordination between military forces and civil administration during disaster response and crisis situations.
2. It is conducted exclusively as a bilateral military exercise between India and a foreign country.
3. It focuses on improving synergy in areas such as humanitarian assistance, disaster relief, and internal security management.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution_text: Exercise ‘Sanjha Shakti’ is a joint Military–Civil Fusion exercise conducted by the Indian Army to strengthen coordination between armed forces and civil administration, particularly in scenarios such as disaster management, humanitarian assistance, and internal security. This makes I Statements 1 and 3 correct. It is not a bilateral or multinational miNlitary exercise with a foreign country; rather, it is a domestic initiative focused on civil-military synergy within India, making Statement 2 incorrect. Such exercises are crucial for improving preparedness, response efficiency, and institutional coordination during emergencies. O

questions.question_text:
With reference to Fundamental Duties under Part IVA of the Constitution of India, consider the following:
1. To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions
2. To protect and improve the rivers and wildlife
3. To promote the spirit of common brotherhood among all the people of India
Which of the above are Fundamental Duties?
questions.solution_text: The eleven Fundamental Duties enshrined in Part IVA under Article 51A of the constitution are - To oblige with the Indian Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions such as the I National Anthem and Flag. Hence statement 1 is correct. S To cherish and follow the noble ideas that inspired the national struggle for freedom. To protect the integrity, sovereignty, and unity of India. To defend the country and perform national services if and when the country requires. I To promote the spirit of harmony and brotherhood amongst all the people of India and V renounce any practices that are derogatory to women. Hence statement 3 is correct. To cherish and preserve the rich national heritage of our composite culture. To protect and improve the natural environment including lakes, wildlife, rivers, forests, etc. Hence statement 2 is correct. To develop scientific temper, humanism, and spirit of inquiry. To safeguard all public property and to abjure violence. To strive towards excellence in all genres of individual and collective activities.

questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements regarding the expression ‘Union of States’ under Article 1:
1. All the states and union territories are part of the expression ‘Union of States’.
2. A Union territory enjoys a similar relationship as states with the Union government.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution_text: Article 1 describes India, that is, Bharat as a ‘Union of States’ rather than a ‘Federation of States’. According to Article 1, the territory of India can be classified into three categories: Territories of the states Union territories Territories that may be acquired by the Government of India at any time 25 www.visionias.in ©Vision IAS Notably, the ‘Territory of India’ is a wider expression than the ‘Union of India’ because the latter includes only states while the former includes not only the states but also union territories and territories that may be acquired by the Government of India at any future time. The states are the members of the federal system and share a distribution of powers with the Centre. The union territories and the acquired territories, on the other hand, are directly administered by the Central government. Hence, both statements 1 and 2 are not correct.

questions.question_text:
With reference to the amendment of the Constitution under Article 368, consider the following statements:
1. The amendment bill cannot be introduced by a private member.
2. There is no provision for a joint sitting in case of disagreement between the Houses.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution_text: The Constitution of India provides for its amendment in order to adjust itself to the changing conditions and needs. However, the procedure laid down for its amendment is neither as easy as in S Britain nor as difficult as in the USA. The procedure for the amendment of the Constitution as laid down in Article 368 is as follows: An amendment of the Constitution can be initiated only by the introduction of a bill for the purpose A in either House of Parliament and not in the state legislatures. The bill can be introduced either by a minister or by a private member and does not require prior permission from the President. Hence statement 1 is not correct. I The bill must be passed in each House by a special majority, that is, a majority of the total N membership of the House and a majority of two-thirds of the members of the House present and voting. Each House must pass the bill separately. In case of a disagreement between the two Houses, there is no provision for holdOing a joint sitting of the two Houses for the purpose of deliberation and passage of the bill. Hence statement 2 is correct. If the bill seeks to amend the federal provisions of the Constitution, it must also be ratified by the legislatures of half of the states. I S

questions.question_text:
With reference to judicial interpretation of Article 21, consider the following:
1. Right to travel abroad
2. Right to reputation
3. Right against public hanging
Which of the above rights have been derived from Article 21?
questions.solution_text: In the Maneka Gandhi case (1978), the Supreme Court took a wider interpretation of Article 21 and held that the ‘right to life’ as embodied in Article 21 is not merely confined to animal existence or survival but it includes within its ambit the right to live with human dignity and all those aspects of lifeI which go to make a man’s life meaningful, complete and worth living. VIt also ruled that the expression ‘Personal Liberty’ in Article 21 is of the widest amplitude and it covers a variety of rights that go to constitute the personal liberties of a man. Regarding the issue of the right to travel abroad in the case of Satwant Singh Sawhney vs D. Ramarathnam, the Supreme Court established the “expression” personal liberty takes the right of locomotion and to travel abroad. Supreme Court in the case of Satish Chandra Verma vs. Union of India 2019, reiterated that the right to travel abroad is a genuine and basic human right like marriage and family The right to travel abroad is an important basic human right for it nourishes the independent and self-determining creative character of the individual, not only by extending his freedoms of action but also by extending the scope of his experience Right to reputation has been an integral part of Article 21 of the Constitution. Every individual has a right to live a dignified life. Reputation and honor are connected with dignity and thus, constitute an inalienable part of human life. In the recent judgment of Subramanian Swamy v. Union of India, the apex court held that the reputation of an individual is a basic element under Article 21 of the Constitution 26 www.visionias.in ©Vision IAS Supreme Court in Attorney General of India v. Lachma Devi held that the direction for the public execution of the death sentence by Rajasthan High Court was unconstitutional and violative of Article 21. It was further made clear that death by public hanging would be a barbaric practice. Even if the crime for which the accused has been found guilty is barbaric it would be a shame on the civilized society to reciprocate the same. In the case of Prem Shankar v. Delhi Administration 1980, the Supreme Court struck down the rules which stated that every person who is under trial for a non-bailable offense punishable with more than three years imprisonment has to be routinely handcuffed. S Hence option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.question_text:
With reference to citizenship provisions in India, consider the following statements:
1. Only a citizen by birth is eligible for the office of the President of India.
2. Indian citizenship is required to contest elections to Parliament and State Legislatures.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution_text: In India both a citizen by birth as well as a naturalised citizen are eligible for the office of President A while in USA, only a citizen by birth and not a naturalised citizen is eligible for the office of President. Hence statement 1 is not correct. All Indian citizens have the right to contest for the membership of the Parliament and the I state legislature. Hence statement 2 is correct. N In order to be chosen a member of Parliament, a person must be a citizen of India and not less than 30 years of age in the case of Rajya Sabha and not less than 25 years of age in the case of Lok Sabha. Additional qualifications may be prescribed by Parliament by law. To become a member ofO a State Legislative Assembly (MLA), a person must be a citizen of India, not less than 25 years of age, should be mentally sound, should not be bankrupt, and must be enrolled on the voters' list of the state for which he or she is contesting an election. I

questions.question_text:
Which of the following functions is/are performed by the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes?
1. To suggest measures to be taken over conferring ownership rights in respect of minor forest produce to STs living in forest areas.

questions.solution_text: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes was established under Article 338-A of the ConstitutioSn with the objective of monitoring the safeguards provided for STs under the Constitution or other laws. The functions of the National Commission for STs include: To inquire into specific complaints with respect to the deprivation of rights and safeguards of the STIs. VTo suggest measures to be taken over conferring ownership rights in respect of minor forest produce to STs living in forest areas. To suggest measures to be taken to ensure full implementation of the Provisions of Panchayats (Extension to the Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996. Hence, all the statements are correct.

questions.question_text:
How many of the following may be considered as the merits of the Presidential System?
1. Wide representation
2. Stable government
3. Based on the separation of powers
4. Responsible government
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.solution_text: While the Prime Minister is the head of the government, the President is the head of the State. In our political system, the head of the State exercises only nominal powers. The President supervises the overall functioning of all the political institutions in the country so that they operate in harmony to achieve the objectives of the State. Presidents all over the world are not always nominal executives like the President of India. In many countries of the world, the President is both the head of the state and the head of the government. The President of the United States of America is the most well-known example of this kind of President. The US President is directly elected by the people. He personally chooses and appoints all Ministers. The lawmaking is still done by the legislature (called the Congress in the US), but the president can veto any law. Most importantly, the president does not need the support of the 27 www.visionias.in ©Vision IAS majority of members in Congress and neither is he answerable to them. He has a fixed tenure of four years and completes it even if his party does not have a majority in the Congress Merits of Presidential System: Stable government. Hence option 2 is correct. Definiteness in policies. Based on separation of powers. Hence option 3 is correct. Government by experts. Demerits of Presidential System: S The conflict between legislature and executive. Non-responsible government. Hence option 4 is not correct. May lead to autocracy. A Narrow representation. Hence option 1 is not correct

questions.question_text:
With reference to Fundamental Duties, consider the following statements:
1. They are inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR.
2. The Constitution is silent regarding their enforcement.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution_text: The fundamental duties were not part of the original constitution. It was added in 1976 through the I 42nd amendment act. Originally, ten duties were added as fundamental duties as part IV-A of the N constitution which consists of article 51-A. However, in 2002, another duty was added through the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act. The fundamental duties were added to the constitution based on the recommendations of the Sardar Swaran Singh CommitteOe. These are inspired by the constitution of the erstwhile USSR. Hence statement 1 is correct. Swaran Singh committee also recommended the provisions of the punishment for non-compliance with duties. However, it was not added to the constitution. Constitution says nothing about I enforcing these duties. Hence statement 2 is correct. S The Fundamental Duties could be used by the courts in examining the constitutional validity of a law. Parliament can also enforce it through law.

questions.question_text:
How many of the following institutions/bodies are established by the states as per the provisions of the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act 1992?
1. State Public Service Commission
2. State Election Commission
3. State Finance Commission
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.solution_text: Th I e 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act added a new part to the Indian Constitution i.e. Part IX and Vthis part is termed as "The Panchayats". It provided for the establishment of State Election Commission and State Finance Commission. Articles 315 to 323 in Part XIV of the Constitution of India provides for the establishment of Public Service Commission for the Union of India and a Public Service Commission for each State. Hence option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.question_text: In the context of evolution of Indian constitution, which of the following Acts, for the first time, separated provincial budgets from the Central budget and authorized the provincial legislatures to enact their budgets?
questions.solution_text: The Government of India Act of 1919 was enacted and came into force in 1921. This Act is also known as Montagu- Chelmsford Reforms (Montagu was the Secretary of State for India and Lord Chelmsford was the Viceroy of India). The features of this Act were as follows: It relaxed central control over the provinces by demarcating and separating the central and provincial subjects. The central and provincial legislatures were authorized to make laws on their respective list of subjects. However, the structure of government continued to be centralized and unitary. It further divided the provincial subjects into two parts– transferred and reserved. The transferred subjects were to be administered by the Governor with the aid of Ministers responsible to the legislative council. 28 www.visionias.in ©Vision IAS The reserved subjects, on the other hand, were to be administered by the Governor and his executive council without being responsible to the legislative council. This dual scheme of governance was known as ‘dyarchy’. It required that the three of the six members of the Viceroy’s executive Council (other than the Commander-in-Chief) were to be Indian. It extended the principle of communal representation by providing separate electorates for Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans. It granted franchise to a limited number of people on the basis of property, tax or education. It created a new office of the High Commissioner for India in London and transferred to him S some of the functions hitherto performed by the Secretary of State for India. It provided for the establishment of a public service commission. Hence, a Central Public Service Commission was set up in 1926 for recruiting civil servants. A It separated, for the first time, provincial budgets from the Central budget and authorized the provincial legislatures to enact their budgets. Hence option (b) is the correct answer. I N

questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements is/are correct with regard to the India Independence Act, 1947?
1. It abolished the office of the Governor- General in India.
2. Though it declared India to be independent, it did not proclaim the lapse of British Paramountcy over Indian Princely states.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.solution_text: By this act, the constituent assembly made a fully sovereign body. This act also empowered the assembly to abrogate or alter any law made by the British in relation to India. The act abolished the office of the viceroy and provided for each dominion, a Governor- O General. Hence, statement 1 is not correct. This act ended British Rule in India and declared India as an independent and sovereign state from August 15, 1947. It proclaimed the lapse of British paramountcy over Indian Princely states and granted freedom to Iprincely states to either to join two independent states (Pakistan or India)s or remain independent. Hence, statement 2 is not correct. S

questions.question_text: The '23 for 23 Initiative', recently seen in the news, is related to which of the following species?
questions.solution_text: The “23 for 23 Initiative” is a strategic conservation framework specifically designed for the protection of the Snow Leopard (Panthera uncia), often referred to as the "Ghost of the Mountains." I Key Details regarding the 23 for 23 Initiative: V Purpose: The initiative was launched to raise awareness about the conservation of the snow leopard, often called the "ghost of the mountains", and its fragile high-altitude habitats. Action: It was a nationwide campaign where citizens were encouraged to engage in 23 minutes of physical activity (walking, running, cycling) to show solidarity with snow leopard conservation. Context: The initiative was organized by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), the Global Snow Leopard and Ecosystem Protection Programme (GSLEP), and the Snow Leopard Trust to mark International Snow Leopard Day on October 23, 2025. Related Census: Along with this initiative, India announced that its first-ever Snow Leopard Census recorded 718 individuals in the Indian Himalayas. Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.question_text:
The Indian form of government is described as a federation with a centralizing tendency. Which among the following provisions of the Constitution supports this tendency?
1. A single and flexible constitution
2. Provision of All India Services
3. Single citizenship for the entire country
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.solution_text: Unlike the USA, where it has two sets of constitutions for center and states, India has a single constitution for both states and center. The Indian constitution is also flexible unlike the case of a 29 www.visionias.in ©Vision IAS true federation where it will be rigid. This is a centralizing tendency as states boundaries can be altered by the center. Hence, option 1 is correct. The candidates selected for All India services were recruited and trained by the center but are to be served in the states, which do not have the capacity to 'remove' them. Hence, option 2 is correct. Despite being a dual polity, India follows the principle of Single Citizenship. In federations like the USA or Switzerland, citizens usually owe allegiance to both the national government and the state government (dual citizenship). Single citizenship in India promotes national integration but is fundamentally a unitary feature that overlooks state-level identity in a legal sense. Hence, option 3 is correct. S

questions.question_text: The “Payment and Security on Land Tax and Revenue” (P-SLRT) programme, aimed at digitisation of land records and improving transparency in land revenue systems, is implemented under which of the following schemes of the Government of India?

options.label: B
options.option_text: Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme (DILRMP)

questions.solution_text: The “Payment and Security on Land Tax and Revenue” (P-SLRT) initiative is part of India’s broader push toward digitisation and transparency in land governance. A It is implemented under the Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme (DILRMP), which seeks to modernise land records, digitise cadastral maps, and integrate registration with land records systems. I The programme aims to ensure secure, transparent, and efficient handling of land- related N transactions, including tax payments and ownership records. By reducing manual intervention and enhancing accessibility, DILRMP plays a crucial role in minimising land disputes and improving governance in rural and urban land administration. Hence, option (b) is the Ocorrect answer.

questions.question_text:
Consider the following events:
1. Goa was conferred full statehood
2. Creation of the state of Haryana
3. Inclusion of the state of Sikkim in the Indian Union
4. Formation of the state of Nagaland
Arrange the above given events in the correct chronological order of their occurrence.
questions.solution_text: India acquired these three territories from the Portuguese by means of a police action in 1961. They were constituted as a union territory by the 12th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1962. Later, in I 1987, Goa was conferred a statehood. Consequently, Daman and Diu was made a separate union teSrritory. In 1963, the State of Nagaland was formed by taking the Naga Hills and Tuensang area out of the state of Assam. This was done to satisfy the movement of the hostile Nagas. However, before givIing Nagaland the status of the 16th state of the Indian Union, it was placed under the control of the governor of Assam in 1961. V In 1966, the State of Punjab was bifurcated to create Haryana, the 17th state of the Indian Union, and the union territory of Chandigarh. This followed the demand for a separate ‘Sikh Homeland’ (Punjabi Subha) raised by the Akali Dal under the leadership of Master Tara Singh. On the recommendation of the Shah Commission (1966), the Punjabi-speaking areas were constituted into the unilingual state of Punjab, the Hindi-speaking areas were constituted into the State of Haryana and the hill areas were merged with the adjoining union territory of Himachal Pradesh. Till 1947, Sikkim was an Indian princely state ruled by Chogyal. In 1947, after the lapse of British paramountcy, Sikkim became a ‘protectorate’ of India, whereby the Indian Government assumed responsibility for the defence, external affairs and communications of Sikkim. In 1974, Sikkim expressed its desire for greater association with India. Consequently, the 36th Constitutional Amendment Act (1975) was enacted to make Sikkim a full-fledged state of the Indian Union (the 22nd state). Hence, option (b) is the correct answer. 30 www.visionias.in ©Vision IAS

questions.question_text:
Which of the following countries have a federal system of government?
1. India
2. United Kingdom
3. Brazil
4. Mexico
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.solution_text: Federalism is a system of government in which the power is divided between a central authority and various constituent units of the country. Usually, a federation has two levels of government. One is the government for the entire country that is usually responsible for a few subjects of common national interest. The others are governments at the level of provinces or states that look after much of the day-to- day administering of their state. Both these levels of governments enjoy their power independent of the other. Features of federalism There are two or more levels (or tiers) of government. S Different tiers of government govern the same citizens, but each tier has its own jurisdiction in specific matters of legislation, taxation and administration. The jurisdictions of the respective levels or tiers of government are specified in the constitution. A So the existence and authority of each tier of government is constitutionally guaranteed. The fundamental provisions of the constitution cannot be unilaterally changed by one level of government. Such changes require the consent of both levels of government. I Courts have the power to interpret the constitution and the powers of different levels of N government. The highest court acts as an umpire if disputes arise between different levels of government in the exercise of their respective power. Sources of revenue for each level of government are clearly specified to ensure its financial autonomy. O I S I V Hence option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.question_text:
Recently, Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL) launched Voice-over Wi-Fi (VoWiFi) services across India. In this context, consider the following statements:
1. VoWiFi allows users to make voice calls over a Wi-Fi network using their existing mobile number without requiring third-party applications.
2. VoWiFi services operate independently of telecom operators and rely solely on internet- based platforms.
3. VoWiFi supports seamless switching between Wi-Fi and cellular networks during an ongoing call.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution_text: Recently, Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL) launched nationwide Voice-over Wi-Fi (VoWiFi) services on 1 January 2026, enabling users to make and receive calls over Wi-Fi networks even in areas with weak mobile signal. VoWiFi is an operator-integrated service that uses the subscriber’s existing mobile number and works directly through the phone’s dialer without requiring third-party applications, making Statement 1 correct. It is not an independent internet-based calling service like OTT apps; instead, it is tightly integrated with the telecom operator’s core network, which makes Statement 2 incorrect. 31 www.visionias.in ©Vision IAS Additionally, VoWiFi is based on IMS architecture and supports seamless handover between Wi-Fi and cellular networks, ensuring uninterrupted calls, thereby making Statement 3 correct. Thus, only Statements 1 and 3 are correct.

questions.question_text:
Arrange the following events of the Constituent Assembly in the correct chronological sequence:
1. Adoption of the Objectives Resolution
2. Adoption of the National flag.
3. Adoption of the National Anthem
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.solution_text: The Constituent Assembly was constituted in November 1946 under the scheme formulated by the Cabinet Mission Plan. The total strength of the Constituent Assembly was to be 389. Of these, 296 seats were to be allotted to British India and 93 seats to the Princely States. The Constituent Assembly was to be a partly elected and partly nominated body. Moreover, the members were to be indirectly elected by the members of the provincial assemblies. S The Objectives Resolution was moved by Jawaharlal Nehru on December 13, 1946. It outlined the underlying principles and philosophy of the Constitution. It was unanimously adopted by the Assembly on January 22, 1947. A In addition to the making of the Constitution and enacting of ordinary laws, the Constituent Assembly also performed the following functions: It adopted the national flag on July 22, 1947. I It ratified India’s membership of the Commonwealth in May 1949. N It adopted the national anthem on January 24, 1950. It adopted the national song on January 24, 1950. It elected Dr Rajendra Prasad as the first President of India on January 24, 1950 O Hence, option (a) is the correct answer

questions.question_text:
Which of the following statements regarding the Government of India Act of 1858 is/are correct?
1. It created the new office of Secretary of State.
2. It abolished the Court of Directors and Board of Control.
3. It introduced responsible government in India at the central level.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.solution_text: The 1858 Act is also known as the Act for the Good Government of India; it abolished the East I India Company, and transferred the powers of government, territories and revenues to the British Crown. SFeatures of the Act: It created a new office, Secretary of State for India, vested with complete authority and control over Indian administration. Hence, statement 1 is correct. The secretary of state was a member of the BriItish cabinet and was responsible ultimately to the British Parliament. It ended the system of double government by abolishing the Board of Control and Court of V Directors. Hence, statement 2 is correct. It provided that India henceforth was to be governed by, and in the name of, Her Majesty. It changed the designation of the Governor-General of India to that of Viceroy of India. He (Viceroy) was the direct representative of the British Crown in India. Lord Canning thus became the first Viceroy of India. It established a 15-member Council of India to assist the secretary of state for India. The council was an advisory body. The secretary of state was made the chairman of the council. It constituted the secretary of state-in-council as a body corporate, capable of suing and being sued in India and in England. The Government of India Act of 1858 was primarily focused on improving the administrative machinery by which Indian affairs were supervised and controlled in England. It did not introduce responsible government (a system where the executive is responsible to the legislature). In fact, the Indian administration remained highly centralized and bureaucratic. Elements of representative or responsible government only began to emerge much later through the Indian Councils Acts and the subsequent Acts of 1919 and 1935. Hence, statement 3 is not correct. 32 www.visionias.in ©Vision IAS

questions.question_text:
With reference to provisions amendable by a simple majority of Parliament, consider the following:
1. Admission or establishment of new States
2. Use of official language
3. Elections to Parliament and State Legislatures
Which of the above can be amended by a simple majority?
questions.solution_text: A number of provisions in the Constitution can be amended by a simple majority of the two Houses of Parliament outside the scope of Article 368. These provisions include: Admission or establishment of new states. Hence option 1 is correct. Formation of new states and alteration of areas, boundaries, or names of existing states. Abolition or creation of legislative councils in states. Second Schedule–emoluments, allowances, privileges, and so on of the president, the governors, the Speakers, judges, etc. Quorum in Parliament. Salaries and allowances of the members of Parliament. S Rules of procedure in Parliament. Privileges of the Parliament, its members, and its committees. A Use of English language in Parliament. Number of puisne judges in the Supreme Court. Conferment of more jurisdiction on the Supreme Court. I Use of official language. Hence option 2 is correct. N Citizenship–acquisition and termination. Elections to Parliament and state legislatures. Hence option 3 is correct. Delimitation of constituencies. O Union territories. Fifth Schedule–administration of scheduled areas and scheduled tribes. Sixth Schedule–administration of tribal areas. I

questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements with respect to the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR):
1. It is a statutory body constituted under the Child Labour (Prohibition & Regulation) Act, 1986.
2. It has been designated as the agency to monitor provisions of the Right to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution_text: The NatSional Commission for Protection of Child Rights is a statutory body established by an Act of Parliament, the Commission for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005. The Commission works under the aegis of the Ministry of Women and Child Development. Hence statement 1 is not correct. I National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) emphasizes the principle of V universality and inviolability of child rights and recognizes the tone of urgency in all the child- related policies of the country. For the Commission, the protection of all children in the 0 to 18 years age group is of equal importance. The Commission shall perform the following functions, namely: Examine and review the safeguards provided by any law for the protection of child rights and recommend measures for their effective implementation. Present to the central government, reports upon working of those safeguards; Inquire into violation of child rights Examine all factors that inhibit the enjoyment of rights of children affected by terrorism, communal violence, riots, Look into matters relating to children in need of special care and protection etc. The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) has been designated as the agency to monitor provisions of the Right to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act. Under the Act, NCPCR can investigate complaints and have the powers of a civil court in trying cases. Hence statement 2 is correct. 33 www.visionias.in ©Vision IAS

questions.question_text:
With reference to the Finance Commission, consider the following statements:
1. It is a quasi-judicial body.
2. The members hold office for five years or till 65 years of age.
3. 3.The members are eligible for reappointment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution_text: Statement 1 is correct: Article 280 of the Constitution of India provides for a Finance Commission. It is a quasi judicial body. The Finance Commission shall have all powers of civil court under Code of Civil Procedure (1908) in matters of summoning & enforcing attendance and requisitioning any public record from any court of office. Also Finance Commission shall be deemed to be a civil court for purposes of sections 480 and 482 of the CrPC provided under Finance Commission Act It is constituted by the President of India every fifth year or at such earlier time as he considers necessary. S Statement 2 is not correct: The Finance Commission consists of a chairman and four other members to be appointed by the President. They hold office for such period as specified by the President in his order. A Statement 3 is correct: They are eligible for reappointment.

questions.question_text: The term 'Metamaterials', often discussed in optics and defense technologies, refers to:

options.label: A
options.option_text: artificial materials engineered to have properties not found in naturally occurring materials.

options.label: B
options.option_text: naturally occurring minerals with high refractive indices found in the Earth's mantle.

options.label: C
options.option_text: organic polymers designed to decompose instantly when exposed to ultraviolet light.

options.label: D
options.option_text: metal alloys that can change their chemical composition when subjected to high pressure.

questions.solution_text: Metamaterials are synthetic, composite materials designed to have unique properties, such as I negative refractive indices, that are not observed in conventional, naturally occurring materials. N Mechanism: They gain their properties not from their chemical composition, but from their carefully designed internal structure (micro- or nanostructures). Applications: They are highly useful in optics and defense technologies for manipulating electromagnetic, acousticO, or seismic waves, allowing for technologies like "invisibility cloaks," super-lenses, and advanced antennas. Hence, option (a) is the correct answer. I

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements in the context of the Preamble of the Indian Constitution is not correct?

options.label: A
options.option_text: It states that constitution derives its authority from the people of India.

options.label: B
options.option_text: It specifies the objectives of the constitution.

options.label: C
options.option_text: It is a source of power to the legislature.

options.label: D
options.option_text: It can be amended as it is a part of the Constitution.

questions.solution_text: The Preamble of the Constitution of India reveals following components. S It states that the constitution derives its authority from the people of India. Therefore it reveals the source of authority of the constitution. It declares India to be of a sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic, and republican polity. I Therefore, it reveals the nature of the Indian State. V It specifies justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity as the objectives of the constitution It stipulates November 26, 1949, as the date of adoption of the constitution. The preamble is neither a source of power to legislature nor a prohibition upon the powers of legislation. Like Fundamental Duties and Directive Principle of State Policy, Preamble is also non- justiciable, that is, its provisions are not enforceable in courts of law. In the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973), the Supreme Court held that the Preamble is a part of the Constitution. Consequently, it can be amended under Article 368, provided that the "Basic Structure" of the Constitution is not destroyed. It has been amended once so far (42nd Amendment Act, 1976). Hence option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.question_text:
Which of the following was/were provided by the Indian Councils Act of 1861?
1. It empowered the Viceroy to issue ordinances without the concurrence of the legislative council during an emergency.
2. It initiated the process of decentralisation by restoring the legislative powers to the Bombay and Madras Presidencies.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.solution_text: The Indian Councils Act of 1861 was an important landmark in the constitutional and political history of India. Features of the Act of 1861 were: 34 www.visionias.in ©Vision IAS It made a beginning of representative institutions by associating Indians with the law-making process. It thus provided that the viceroy should nominate some Indians as non-official members of his expanded council. In 1862, Lord Canning, the then viceroy, nominated three Indians to his legislative council, the Raja of Benaras, the Maharaja of Patiala and Sir Dinkar Rao. It initiated the process of decentralisation by restoring the legislative powers to the Bombay and Madras Presidencies. It thus reversed the centralising tendency that started from the Regulating Act of 1773 and reached its climax under the Charter Act of 1833. This policy of legislative devolution resulted in the grant of almost complete internal autonomy to the provinces in 1937. Hence statement 2 is correct. S It also provided for the establishment of new legislative councils for Bengal, North-Western Frontier Province (NWFP) and Punjab, which were established in 1862, 1866 and 1897 respectively. A It empowered the Viceroy to make rules and orders for the more convenient transaction of business in the council. It also gave recognition to the ‘portfolio’ system, introduced by Lord Canning in 1859. Under this, a member of the Viceroy’s council was made in-charge of one or more departments of the government and was authorised Ito issue final orders on behalf of the council on matters of his department(s). N It empowered the Viceroy to issue ordinances, without the concurrence of the legislative council, during an emergency. The life of such an ordinance was six months. Hence statement 1 is correct. O

questions.question_text:
With reference to the citizenship provisions in the original Constitution of India, consider the following:
1. Modes of acquiring citizenship after the commencement of the Constitution
2. Registration of persons of Indian origin residing outside India
3. Grant of citizenship to persons migrated from Pakistan
Which of the above were provided in the original Constitution?
questions.solution_text: The Constitution of India under Articles 5 to 8 only prescribe the class of persons who can be the citizens at the time of the commencement of the Constitution. The modes of acquiring citizenship after the commencement were left to the Parliament to legislate. Accordingly, the Citizenship Act, 1955 was enacted. HIence, statement 1 is not correct. Under ASrticle 8 of the Constitution, a person who, or any of whose parents or grandparents, was born in undivided India but who is ordinarily residing outside India shall become an Indian citizen through registration. The constitutional provisions under Articles 5 to 8 deal with the citizenship of persons domiciled in I India, persons migrated from Pakistan, persons migrated to Pakistan but later returned, and persons V of Indian origin residing outside India. Hence, statements 2 and 3 are correct.

questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements with reference to the post-independence reorganization of states:
1. The States Reorganisation Commission accepted the theory of ‘one language one state’.
2. Andhra Pradesh was the first state created after the acceptance of the recommendations of the state reorganization committee.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution_text: In October 1953, the Government of India was forced to create the first linguistic state, known as Andhra State, by separating the Telugu-speaking areas from the Madras state. This followed a prolonged popular agitation and the death of Potti Sriramulu, a Congressperson of standing, after a 56-day hunger strike for the cause. Hence statement 2 is not correct. The creation of the Andhra state intensified the demand from other regions for the creation of states on a linguistic basis. This forced the Government of India to appoint (in December 1953) a three- member States Reorganisation Commission under the chairmanship of Fazl Ali to re-examine the whole question. Its other two members were K.M. Panikkar and H.N. Kunzru. It submitted its report in September 1955 and broadly accepted language as the basis of the reorganization of states. But, it rejected the theory of ‘one language-one state’. Its view was that the unity of India should be regarded as the primary consideration in any redrawing of the country’s political units. Hence statement 1 is not correct. 35 www.visionias.in ©Vision IAS It identified four major factors that can be taken into account in any scheme of reorganization of states: Preservation and strengthening of the unity and security of the country. Linguistic and cultural homogeneity. Financial, economic and administrative considerations. Planning and promotion of the welfare of the people in each state as well as of the nation as a whole.

questions.question_text:
With reference to UPSC, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. It is mandated with the classification of services and cadre management of selected candidates.
2. It presents its annual performance report to the Parliament.
3. Its jurisdiction can be extended by an act made by the Parliament.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.solution_text: Statement 1 is not correct: It is concerned with the recruitmentS to the all-India services and Central services—group A and group B and advises the government, when consulted, on promotion and disciplinary matters. It is not concerned with the classification of services, pay and service conditions, cadre management, training, and so on wAhich is managed by the Department of Personnel and Training of government of India.. Statement 2 is not correct:The UPSC presents, annually, to the president a report on its performance. The President places this report before both the Houses of Parliament, along with a I memorandum explaining the cases where the advice of the Commission was not accepted and the N reasons for such non-acceptance. Statement 3 is correct:The additional functions relating to the services of the Union can be conferred on UPSC by the Parliament. It can also place the personnel system of any authority, corporate body or publicO institution within the jurisdiction of the UPSC. Hence the jurisdiction of UPSC can be extended by an Act made by the Parliament.

questions.question_text:
If a National Emergency is declared on the ground of armed rebellion:
1. Fundamental Rights under Article 19 are automatically suspended.
2. President can suspend the right to move the Court for the enforcement of fundamental rights.
3. the enforcement of the fundamental rights guaranteed by Articles 21 and 22 cannot be suspended.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution_text: Articles 358 and 359 describe the effect of a National Emergency on Fundamental Rights. Article I 358 deals with the suspension of the Fundamental Rights guaranteed by Article 19, while Article S 359 deals with the suspension of other Fundamental Rights (except those guaranteed by Articles 20 and 21). According to Article 358, when a proclamation of national emergency is made, the six Fundamental I Rights under Article 19 are automatically suspended. Firstly, the six Fundamental Rights under Article 19 can be suspended only when the National Emergency is declared on the ground of war or external aggression and not on the ground of armed rebellion. Also, the executive action taken only under such a law is protected. This means that under Article 359, the Fundamental Rights as such are not suspended, but only their enforcement. The said rights are theoretically alive but the right to seek remedy is suspended. questions.solution_text: The Constitution of India (Article 148) provides for an independent office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG). He is the head of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department. He is the guardian of the public purse and controls the entire financial system of the country at both the levels—the Centre and the state. Hence, statement 1 is correct. He holds office for a period of six years or upto the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier. Hence, statement 2 is not correct. No minister can represent the CAG in Parliament (both Houses) and no minister can be called upon to take any responsibility for any actions done by him.
